items.title: fix: return 412 for matching If-None-Match on non-GET/HEAD in handleCacheHeaders
items.body:
`handleCacheHeaders` returned `304 Not Modified` for every method when the cache validators matched. Per RFC 9110:

- §13.1.2: a matching `If-None-Match` on a method other than GET/HEAD must fail the request with `412 Precondition Failed`, not `304`;
- §13.2.1: conditional headers must be ignored for OPTIONS, TRACE and CONNECT;
- §13.1.3: `If-Modified-Since` must be ignored for methods other than GET/HEAD.

The fix keeps the helper's control-flow contract (returns `true` = stop) while selecting the right status: 304 for GET/HEAD, 412 for a matching `If-None-Match` on other methods, and `false` (handler runs normally) for the ignore cases. Added four tests covering POST/PUT → 412, HEAD → 304, POST + If-Modified-Since-only → 200, and OPTIONS → 200.

Fixes #1623.

items.title: fix(cache): honor request methods when evaluating cache headers
items.body:
resolves #1623

Matching `If-None-Match` preconditions stop POST, PUT, PATCH, and DELETE with `412` rather than `304` ([RFC 9110 §13.1.2](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110#section-13.1.2)). These methods ignore `If-Modified-Since`; OPTIONS, TRACE, and CONNECT ignore conditional headers ([§13.2.1](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110#section-13.2.1)). GET, HEAD, and QUERY retain their existing `304` behavior.

The issue includes a runnable reproduction. Regression tests cover both web and Node adapters, including weak tags, wildcards, nonmatches, and validator overrides; helper-level tests also cover TRACE and CONNECT. They fail with only the source changes reverted.

`pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm build`, and the affected suites passed. Local `pnpm test`: 3,219 passed, 51 skipped, one Node body-limit timeout; unchanged main at f0e1780: 3,128 passed, 51 skipped, two body-limit timeouts, including the same test.

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Conditional cache validation now returns `304 Not Modified` for matching validators on `GET`, `HEAD`, and `QUERY` requests.
  * For other methods, a matching `If-None-Match` returns `412 Precondition Failed`; `If-Modified-Since` does not trigger a conditional response.
  * `CONNECT`, `OPTIONS`, and `TRACE` requests ignore both conditional headers and continue processing.

* **Documentation**
  * Clarified how conditional cache headers are handled across request methods.
